profile_text.body:
Gong is a for-profit startup founded in 2015 and headquartered in Palo Alto, California. The company describes itself as offering a "Revenue AI OS," a platform aimed at go-to-market organizations that it says combines multimodal revenue signal processing, specialized AI agents, and purpose-built applications. Its stated use cases include closing deals faster, predicting pipeline risk, automating handoffs, enabling sales teams at scale, increasing win rates, and predicting churn.

The company's core product, also called Gong, is categorized as a revenue intelligence AI tool covering call analysis, deal coaching, and sales data handling. The platform includes named sub-products such as Gong Engage, described as a sales engagement tool that uses AI to prioritize and personalize communications, and Gong Enable, which includes an AI Trainer feature the company says allows sales teams to build training from recorded customer conversations. A quoted customer on the site reports saving 6,700 hours across call preparation, follow-up, and CRM updates, and attributes a 32% lift in buyer response rates to Gong's AI Tracker agent.

The held facts show Gong has a notable law exposure profile, with 139 cases linked to California. Three MCP server entries are associated with the Gong name in the registry, two focused on SQLite database exploration and one unrelated to Gong's core business, suggesting partial or incidental namespace overlap rather than official Gong-published servers.
